overview: The two halves of every redox reaction — one substance loses electrons while another gains them.
genZNote: Oxidation: losing electrons (and OIL RIG never lets you forget it). Reduction: gaining them.

aspects.label: Electron Change
aspects.valueA: Loss of electrons (or gain of oxygen / loss of hydrogen).
aspects.valueB: Gain of electrons (or loss of oxygen / gain of hydrogen).

aspects.label: Biological Example
aspects.valueA: Glucose is oxidised during cellular respiration, releasing energy.
aspects.valueB: Oxygen is reduced to water at the end of the electron transport chain.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Oxidation and reduction always occur together in a redox reaction — one substance's loss is another's gain.
overlay.memoryTrick: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons).
overlay.commonMisconception: Oxidation doesn't require oxygen to be literally involved — the electron-based definition is the general, correct one.
